extracted.intended_audience: auditors of entities receiving Federal awards and grant/financial managers of non-Federal entities
extracted.subtask_description: Official audit guidance (A-133 Compliance Supplement) describing compliance requirements and suggested audit procedures for testing cost allowability, indirect cost rate proposals/plans, cash management, Davis-Bacon Act compliance, and related provisions for entities that receive Federal funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equitable and consistent allocation of indirect costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost allocation methodology complies with the applicable cost principles and provides equitable and consistent allocation of indirect costs to benefitting cost objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cost allocation bases include all allowable and unallowable base costs to which allowable indirect costs are allocable and the cost allocation methodology produces an equitable and consistent distribution of costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of indirect cost rates per approved agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: Indirect cost rates were applied in accordance with approved rate agreements and associated billings were the result of applying the approved rate to the proper base amount(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select a sample of claims for reimbursement and verify that the rates used are in accordance with the rate agreement, that rates were applied to the appropriate bases, and that the amounts claimed were the product of applying the rate to the applicable base.

rubrics_metrics.name: State/local/tribal cost allocations in accordance with CAPs
rubrics_metrics.description: For States, local governments, and Indian tribal governments, cost allocations were in accordance with CAPs approved by the Federal cognizant agency for indirect cost negotiation or, where plans are not subject to approval, in accordance with the plan on file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify that methods of charging costs to Federal awards are in accordance with the provisions of the approved CAP or prepared CAP on file and for government-wide CAPs ascertain reimbursement amounts were in accordance with approved CAPs or plans on file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost accounting practice disclosures (DS-1/DS-2) reflect actual practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost accounting practice disclosures, described in the DS-1 or DS-2 (including amendments), represented actual practice consistently applied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read the DS-1 or DS-2 and its amendments and ascertain if the disclosures agree with the policies prescribed in the institution's policies and procedures documents; test that the disclosures agree with actual practices for the period covered by audit, including consistency throughout the period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation of review of large research facilities under construction
rubrics_metrics.description: The institution's review of large research facilities under construction was documented as required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For large research facilities under construction of which 40 percent or more of total assignable space is expected for Federal use, review board minutes or other documentation showing Board of Trustees or independent entity review/approval. For facilities costing more than $25 million with 50%+ Federal use, ascertain documentation of review steps to assure construction costs are reasonable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Directly associated costs are unallowable when related cost is unallowable
rubrics_metrics.description: When an unallowable cost is incurred, directly associated costs (costs incurred solely as a result of incurring another cost) are also unallowable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: fringe benefits are directly associated with payroll costs; if the payroll cost is unallowable, the associated fringe benefits are also unallowable. Auditors should be aware and consider directly associated costs when identifying unallowable charges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transactions conform to OMB Basic Guidelines (authorization/legal)
rubrics_metrics.description: For State and local governments, transactions must be authorized or not prohibited under State or local laws or regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test sample transactions for conformance with applicable Basic Guidelines in OMB cost principles circulars, including legality under state/local law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transactions approved by Federal awarding agency when required
rubrics_metrics.description: Transactions were approved by the Federal awarding agency, if required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify approvals where the cost principles or award terms require prior approval by the Federal awarding agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conformance with allowability provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Transactions conform with the allowability of costs provisions of applicable cost principles, or limitations in the program agreement, program regulations, or program statute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test that costs charged are allowable under the applicable cost principles and any program-specific limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conformance with allocability provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Transactions conform with the allocability provisions of applicable cost principles or CASE Standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure costs are allocable to the award in accordance with principles (i.e., benefit the award and be assignable in proportions that can be approximated using reasonable methods).

rubrics_metrics.name: Charges represent actual costs (not budgeted/projections)
rubrics_metrics.description: Charges represent charges for actual costs, not budgeted or projected amounts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test sampled charges to supporting documentation showing actual incurrence rather than estimates or projections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fringe benefit allocations based on benefits received by employee classes
rubrics_metrics.description: With respect to fringe benefit allocations, charges, or rates, such allocations, charges, or rates are based on the benefits received by different classes of employees within the organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review fringe benefit allocation bases to ensure they reflect benefits by employee classes (e.g., salaried vs. hourly).

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniform application to Federal and non-Federal activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs are applied uniformly to Federal and non-Federal activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify costs are treated consistently between Federal and non-Federal activities to avoid cross-subsidization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency in accounting treatment across periods
rubrics_metrics.description: Given consistent accounting treatment within and between accounting periods: costs incurred for the same purpose, in like circumstances, be treated as either direct costs only or indirect costs only with respect to final cost objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check accounting classifications across periods to ensure consistency in classifying costs as direct or indirect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Costs calculated in conformity with CASE Standards/GAAP/other basis
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs are calculated in conformity with CASE Standards, generally accepted accounting principles, or another comprehensive basis of accounting, when required under the applicable cost principles or CASE Standards. Costs for post-employment benefits must be funded to be allowable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure calculations follow required accounting standards; verify funding of post-employment benefits where required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Costs not used to meet cost-sharing for other federally-supported activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Not included as a cost or used to meet cost sharing requirements of other Federally-supported activities of the current or a prior period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test that costs claimed are not being double-counted to satisfy cost-sharing or matching requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Costs net of applicable credits
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs are net of all applicable credits, e.g., volume or cash discounts, insurance recoveries, refunds, rebates, trade-ins, adjustments for checks not cashed, and scrap sales.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify that claimed costs have been reduced by any applicable credits or recoveries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Costs not charged both directly and as component of indirect costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Not included as both a direct billing and as a component of indirect costs, e.g., excluded from cost pools included in CAPs and/or EDCRPs, if charged directly to Federal awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure no double charging by confirming items billed directly are excluded from indirect cost bases or pools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Costs supported by appropriate documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs are supported by appropriate documentation, such as approved purchase orders, receiving reports, vendor invoices, canceled checks, and time and attendance records, and correctly charged as to account, amount, and period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documentation requirements for salaries and wages, and time and effort distribution are described in applicable cost principles. Documentation may be in electronic form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal/central service charges comply with cost principles
rubrics_metrics.description: When material charges are made from internal service, central service, pension, or similar activities or funds, the charges are in accordance with the applicable cost principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider procedures such as testing retained earnings/fund balances, working capital levels, refunds of transfers, billing consistency, exclusion of unallowable costs from billing rates, and proper rate development/adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retained earnings/fund balances computed in accordance with cost principles
rubrics_metrics.description: For activities accounted for in separate funds ascertain if retained earnings/fund balances (including reserves) were computed in accordance with the applicable cost principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review computation of retained earnings and reserves for compliance with cost principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Working capital not excessive for internal service funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Working capital was not excessive in amount (generally not greater than 60 days for cash expenses for normal operations incurred for the period exclusive of depreciation, capital costs and debt principal costs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess working capital balances and reasonableness relative to operational cash needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refunds to Federal Government for improper transfers/borrows
rubrics_metrics.description: Refunds were made to the Federal Government for its share of any amounts transferred or borrowed from internal service or central service funds for purposes other than to meet the operating liabilities, including interest on debt, of the fund.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test for appropriate refunds where funds were used for other than the fund's operating liabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistent billing to all users of internal services
rubrics_metrics.description: All users of services are billed in a consistent manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test that billing practices are consistent across service users and periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Billing rates exclude unallowable costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Billing rates exclude unallowable costs, in accordance with applicable cost principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test that unallowable cost items are not included in billing/rate calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Billing rates developed on actual costs and adjusted to eliminate profits
rubrics_metrics.description: Where activities are not accounted for in separate funds, billing rates (or charges) are developed based on actual costs and were adjusted to eliminate profits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify rate development methods and adjustments made to remove profit elements when required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actuarial studies for self-insurance and pension-type programs
rubrics_metrics.description: For organizations that have self-insurance and certain types of fringe benefit programs (e.g., pension funds), independent actuarial studies appropriate for such activities are performed at least biennially and current period costs were allocated based on an appropriate study which is not over two years old.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain and review actuarial study documentation and verify allocations are based on current study results.

rubrics_metrics.name: IDCRP/IDCRA testing to provide assurance on cost pools and allocation methods
rubrics_metrics.description: When an IDCRA is the basis for material charges to a major program, the auditor is required to obtain appropriate assurance that the costs collected in the cost pools and allocation methods are in compliance with the applicable cost principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptable options include: perform interim testing of costs charged to cost pools during the base year audit; test costs charged to cost pools underlying the IDCRP during the year immediately following the base year; or test when charges become material (but earlier testing is encouraged). If prior testing exists, test only for material changes to cost accounting practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ascertain prior testing and material changes for IDCRP
rubrics_metrics.description: Ascertain if the IDCRP has been tested in a prior year and whether prior testing provides appropriate audit assurance; if prior testing provides assurance, further review not required unless material changes occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inquire of auditee management about changes to cost accounting practices; if material changes occur and the auditee is required to file the IDCRP with a Federal cognizant agency, ascertain if the agency has been notified. For non-Federal entities required to file DS-1/DS-2, perform testing under DS-1/DS-2 requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test cost pools underlying IDCRP/CAP include only allowable costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Test the cost pools which form the basis of the IDCRP/CAP and the resulting charges to Federal awards to ascertain if they include only allowable costs in accordance with the cost principles or CASE Standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested audit procedure number 1 provides specific tests (see documentation, invoices, payroll, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Test allocation methods for conformity and equitable distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Test the methods of allocating the costs to ascertain if they are in accordance with the provisions of the cost principles or CASE Standards and produce an equitable distribution of costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed tests may include: (1) test statistical data (square footage, case counts, salaries/wages) to ascertain reasonableness and completeness; (2) review time studies or time and effort reports for mathematical/statistical accuracy and basis on actual effort; (3) review allocation methodology for consistency and test appropriateness of methods used to make changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Testing CAPs annually when costs are material to a major program
rubrics_metrics.description: Since costs allocated through CAPs may include current year and prior year costs, the auditor should test the costs charged to cost pools supporting CAPs and the methods of allocating costs from CAPs in each year when these costs are material to a major program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply similar procedures as IDCRP testing: test cost pools, allocation methods, statistical bases, time studies, and allocation methodology consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obtain/read current IDCRA/CAP and determine terms in effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Obtain and read the current Indirect Cost Rate Agreement (IDCRA) and/or CAP and determine the terms in effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the agreement/plan terms to guide testing (e.g., applicable bases, exclusions, approved rates).

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify rates and application to appropriate bases for reimbursement claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Select a sample of claims for reimbursement and verify that the rates used are in accordance with the rate agreement, that rates were applied to the appropriate bases, and that the amounts claimed were the product of applying the rate to the applicable base.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also verify that the costs included in the bases are consistent with the costs that were included in the base year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Assistance CAPs: verify methods of charging per approved CAP
rubrics_metrics.description: For Public Assistance CAPs (States, local governments, and Indian tribal governments only), verify that the methods of charging costs to Federal awards are in accordance with the provisions of the approved CAP or prepared CAP on file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review CAP documentation and test charges to Federal awards for consistency with CAP terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: State and local government-wide CAPs: reimbursement of central service costs per CAP
rubrics_metrics.description: Ascertain if the amounts used for reimbursement of central service costs for Federal awards were in accordance with the approved CAPs or plans on file, when approval is not required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trace reimbursement calculations and supporting costs to CAP provisions or plan documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: DS-1/DS-2: disclosures agree with policies and actual practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Read the DS-1 or DS-2 and its amendments and ascertain if the disclosures agree with the policies prescribed in the institution's policies and procedures documents; test that the disclosures agree with actual practices for the period covered by audit, including whether the practices were consistent throughout the period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For non-Federal entities required to submit DS-1 or DS-2, this objective applies and testing is performed in Step 6 'DS-1 and DS-2 Requirements.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Audit objective: minimize time between Federal fund transfer and disbursement
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether the recipient/subrecipient followed procedures to minimize the time elapsing between the transfer of funds from the U.S. Treasury, or pass-through entity, and their disbursement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested audit procedures include sampling cash draws and verifying timing, reviewing clearance patterns for Treasury-State Agreement programs, and tracing reimbursement requests to paid costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: States comply with Treasury-State Agreement or Subpart B procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether States have complied with the terms and conditions of the Treasury-State Agreement or Subpart B procedures prescribed by Treasury.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify which programs are covered per materiality thresholds, determine funding techniques used, and review clearance patterns for conformance to the Treasury-State Agreement (31 CFR sections 205.7–205.9).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pass-through entities monitor subrecipient cash draws and reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether the pass-through entity implemented procedures to assure that subrecipients conformed substantially to the same stand ards of timing and amount as apply to the pass-through entity, and established procedures to ensure receipt of reports on subrecipients' cash balances and disbursements in sufficient time for reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select representative sample of subrecipients and ascertain procedures implemented; test subrecipient cash draws for conformity to procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interest earned on advances reported/remitted as required
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether interest earned on advances was reported/remitted as required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review calculation of interest obligation (e.g., annual reports submitted by State), trace amounts used in calculation to supporting documentation, and verify remittance/timeliness. Note thresholds: local governments remit interest promptly at least quarterly; non-State nonprofit entities remit interest in excess of $250 to HHS Payment Management System; local governments may keep up to $100 per year for admin expenses.

rubrics_metrics.name: States: verify funding techniques and clearance patterns for covered programs
rubrics_metrics.description: For programs tested as major for States, verify which programs are covered by the Treasury-State Agreement and determine the funding techniques used; for techniques requiring clearance patterns, review supporting documentation and verify clearance pattern conforms to requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Appendix A to subpart A of 31 CFR part 205 to identify coverage, and test clearance patterns per 31 CFR sections 205.8 and 205.9(b)(4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reimbursement requests: costs paid prior to reimbursement request
rubrics_metrics.description: Select a sample of reimbursement requests and trace to supporting documentation showing that the costs for which reimbursement was requested were paid prior to the date of the reimbursement request (31 CFR section 205.7(c)(5)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicable to programs on reimbursement basis; test that recipient paid costs before requesting reimbursement from the Federal Government.

rubrics_metrics.name: For passed-through Federal draws: subrecipients minimize draw-to-disbursement time
rubrics_metrics.description: For programs where Federal cash draws are passed through to subrecipients, ascertain procedures implemented to assure subrecipients minimize time between transfer from recipient and payout for program purposes, and select samples to test conformity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A-102 Common Rule § .37(a)(4) requires procedures; test representative samples of draws by subrecipients and verify they conformed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other recipients/subrecipients: established procedures to minimize draw-disbursement time
rubrics_metrics.description: For programs which received advances of Federal funds, ascertain the procedures established with the Federal agency or pass-through entity to minimize the time between the transfer of Federal funds and the payout of funds for program purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select a sample of Federal cash draws and verify established procedures were followed and that available program income/rebates/refunds were used before requesting additional cash payments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review records to determine interest earned on Federal cash draws and remittance
rubrics_metrics.description: Review records to determine if interest was earned on Federal cash draws and if so, review evidence to ascertain whether it was returned to the appropriate agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check accounting records and remittance evidence; include threshold considerations in guidance (e.g., $100 administrative allowance, $250 remittance rule for non-State nonprofits).

rubrics_metrics.name: Davis-Bacon Act: ensure prevailing wages paid on covered construction contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: When required by the Davis-Bacon Act or implementing regulations, all laborers and mechanics employed by contractors or subcontractors to work on construction contracts in excess of $2000 financed by Federal assistance funds must be paid wages not less than those established for the locality by DOL.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audit objective: determine whether the non-Federal entity ensured contractors and subcontractors paid prevailing wage rates. Suggested procedures: ascertain coverage of projects, select sample of contracts/subcontracts and verify inclusion of required prevailing wage clauses, determine applicable prevailing wage determinations, and examine contractor/subcontractor payrolls and certifications for compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Davis-Bacon: include required prevailing wage clause in contracts > $2000
rubrics_metrics.description: Verify that the required prevailing wage rate clauses were included in contracts for construction which exceed $2000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select a sample of construction contracts and subcontracts to confirm required clauses are present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Davis-Bacon: determine applicable prevailing wage rates
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine the prevailing wage rates applicable at the time of the construction payroll (DOL Wage and Hour Division Register of Wage Determinations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use DOL published wage determinations or online Davis-Bacon databases to obtain appropriate rates for locality and time period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Davis-Bacon: examine payrolls and certifications for compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine a sample of contractor or subcontractor payroll submissions and certifications and ascertain if such submissions indicate that laborers and mechanics were paid the prevailing wage rates established by the DOL for the locality at the time of the construction payroll.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review payrolls, certified statements, and supporting documentation to verify wage payments match required DOL rates.
